title: 85mm Portrait
description: An 85mm portrait in 85mm cinematography is a short telephoto used from a farther stand so a head-and-shoulders stays large while the background enlarges and recedes in importance. The person becomes the landscape; the room becomes stacked color and shape behind them.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Walk back until an 85mm fills the frame with a face. Noses stop dominating.
Ears sit in proportion. The wall behind them comes forward as a soft plane rather than a readable room.
Isolation is the job: a person is the country, and everyone else is weather. It is the wrong tool for geography.

You cannot hold a kitchen two-shot honestly at 85mm in a small room because you cannot get far enough, and if you could, the space would flatten into wallpaper. If the beat is person plus place, go to 35mm Moderate Wide or 24mm Wide.
If the beat is surveillance from across a street, you wanted 135mm Telephoto.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Stand first, farther than conversation. Restore subject size with 85mm.

That distant viewpoint is what compresses facial features and enlarges background objects; the 85mm only chooses the crop. Open the aperture if you want rapid falloff, but shallow focus is a separate choice from the length.
Keep the camera at eye height unless you mean a power tilt. Prompt: 85mm portrait of [Subject], compressed background, rapid falloff, isolation, the face as the only country.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a person is the landscape: a close-up of thought, a romantic single, a face that should not share billing with the room. Do not use it for masters, group geography, or any beat that still needs architecture as a partner.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Her often isolates faces against a soft city so the person is the only country in the frame. Portrait cinema in general uses short telephotos this way: farther stand, larger face, background as a plane.
Borrow the distance and the isolation, not a still of Joaquin Phoenix.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is 50mm Normal or a wide close-up that balloons the nose. The tell is a large room still readable behind a close face, or a stretched forehead from standing too close with short glass.
Fix: walk back, 85mm, face large, background stacked and secondary.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is 85mm portrait in film?
It is a short telephoto used from a farther stand so a face stays large while the background enlarges and loses importance. The person reads as the landscape.
85mm Portrait vs 50mm Normal
50mm at talking distance still shows a honest room. 85mm from farther back compresses that room into a plane and isolates the face. Same crop size, different stand, different space.
When should I use 85mm portrait?
Use it when the face is the scene and the room should not compete. Skip it for geography, two-shots in small rooms, and environmental portraits.
How do I prompt 85mm portrait for AI image or video?
Write: 85mm portrait of [Subject], compressed background, rapid falloff, isolation, the face as the only country. Specify head-and-shoulders. Forbid wide stretch and readable architecture.
